## Why

Checks 01 to 07 tested one skill at a time, with hints. This one tests whether Positron has become the tool you reach for without thinking.

It is one ordinary Coursera lab, done start to finish, with a clock running and the docs closed.

## The rules

- One full Coursera lab, from opening the folder to the final commit.
- RStudio and VS Code stay closed.
- No Positron docs unless you are stuck for more than five minutes. Log every lookup.
- No AI features.
- The R half is capped at 20 minutes, as always.

**Time box:** the lab's own time, plus 20 minutes for R, plus 10 for this file.

## Python half: the lab

Do the lab. As you go, tick each thing you did without looking anything up.

- [ ] Opened the repository and landed in the right environment
- [ ] Opened the lab notebook on the right kernel
- [ ] Inspected the data in the Data Explorer
- [ ] Used the Variables pane instead of printing
- [ ] Found an earlier plot and traced it to its code
- [ ] Opened help for a function inside Positron
- [ ] Formatted code with the formatter
- [ ] Used the debugger or the Console to chase at least one error
- [ ] Committed the finished lab from inside Positron

**End time for the Python half:**

## R half (20-minute cap)

On the lab's dataset, write a short R Quarto document with one table and one plot, render it, and commit it.

- [ ] Started an R session beside the Python one
- [ ] Viewed the data in the Data Explorer from R
- [ ] Ran cells and saw output where I expected it
- [ ] Formatted with Air
- [ ] Rendered to HTML
- [ ] Committed
